title: Rubble-pile dynamic evolution and kinematics: DEM porosity field, force-chain network and mu(I) rheology calibration
decision: Decide whether a DEM-calibrated quadratic mu(I) = mu0 + alpha I + beta I^2 law, together with the conservative porosity field phi(x,t) and the force-chain statistics (Z, A_c), is admissible as the equivalent-continuum input of the broken-ice channel-resistance model, i.e. whether all five machine-checkable acceptance criteria of the battle node hold simultaneously.

alternatives.primary: quadratic mu(I) = mu0 + alpha I + beta I^2 fitted on the pooled three-scenario dataset (as specified by the battle node)
alternatives.secondary_per_scenario: the same quadratic fit per scenario, reported as a collapse-consistency check (does one law describe shear, compression and channel flow?)
rejected_null_hypotheses: mu is rate independent in the sampled I range (alpha = beta = 0): rejected if the quadratic fit's F-like evidence (R^2) exceeds the declared threshold
mu(I) is undefined without contacts (a contact-free state yields mu = 0): rejected by construction, the code must raise

hypothesis: In the sampled inertial-number range the DEM rubble pile follows a rate-dependent friction law with a positive slope, its measured friction level is compatible with the ice-rubble literature band (mu ~ 0.2-0.7), and the resulting equivalent viscosity at the declared reference state falls inside the ice-debris anchor window.

metrics.A_porosity_conservation: |int(phi) dA / A - phi_global| from the stored field vs an independently computed global porosity
metrics.B_force_chain_partition: n_strong + n_weak - n_total and |sum f_strong + sum f_weak - sum f| / sum f
metrics.C_fit_quality: R^2 and residual standard deviation of the quadratic mu(I) least-squares fit
metrics.D_viscosity: eta = mu(I) P / gamma_dot at the declared reference state
metrics.E_negative_control: contact-free state must raise RubbleNoContactsError/RubbleRheologyError instead of returning 0

unit_of_analysis: one DEM run (a scenario at one imposed rate and one seed); the run value is the mean over its steady-state snapshots, the run uncertainty is the standard error over those snapshots. Per-snapshot values are stored for audit but are not the fit unit (they are strongly autocorrelated).

baseline_and_control.porosity: negative control corrupts the stored field (drops one boundary row/column, i.e. mimics a missing periodic-wrap or wall-clipping term) and must fail the 1e-6 audit; the uncorrupted field must pass
baseline_and_control.force_chain: negative control feeds overlapping strong/weak masks and must report n_overlap > 0 and passed = false
baseline_and_control.rheology: negative control feeds a contact-free configuration (single isolated disk from the real engine) and must raise, not return 0
baseline_and_control.fit: synthetic ground-truth law mu = 0.55 + 0.80 I - 1.10 I^2 must be recovered to 1e-8 by the fitter

thresholds_declared_before_production_ru.D_window_source: Guimaraes et al. 2022 ice-debris-flow rheology order-of-magnitude window declared in the battle node (digitised per-point comparison WITHHELD)
thresholds_declared_before_production_ru.fit_scope: pooled over all three scenarios (acceptance applies to the pooled law); per-scenario fits are a consistency diagnostic only

controlled: particle-size distribution (bidisperse), inter-particle friction mu = 0.5, rolling friction 0.05, contact stiffness kn = 3e4 N/m, thickness 0.03 m, density 917 kg/m3, wall friction (same mu)
packing preparation (radius growth from a dilute RSA packing to the target solid fraction)
post-processing grid h = 5 d50, 80 % force quantile split
varied: imposed rate (5 shear rates, 3 compression rates, 3 drift speeds)
solid fraction (shear 0.82, compression starts at 0.80 and densifies, channel 0.80)
confounders: wall slip and shear banding (the measured bulk rate differs from the nominal one; only the measured rate enters I)
densification during compression (phi and P drift within a run)
finite-size stress fluctuations (N ~ 300 disks; reduced by snapshot averaging and 2 seeds)
inter-scenario structural offsets (wall friction, hull geometry) which are expected to appear as a scatter around one pooled law and are reported, not smoothed away
exclusions_declared: snapshots with fewer than 20 bulk particles are skipped (profile not defined)
snapshots whose bulk contact network is empty raise by design and therefore cannot enter
no exclusion based on the observed mu or I values; no post-hoc outlier removal

repetitions: shear: 5 rates x 2 seeds; compression: 3 rates x 2 seeds; channel: 3 speeds x 2 seeds. Two seeds is the minimum that separates a rate trend from a preparation artefact at affordable cost; the standard error over the steady-state snapshots is reported for every run and propagated into the fit diagnostics.

environment.determinism: every scenario seeds its packing and the engine is deterministic (fixed dt, no random forces); two seeds differ only in the packing realisation

analysis.fit: ordinary least squares on the design matrix [1, I, I^2] over the run-mean points; R^2 = 1 - SS_res/SS_tot; residual_std = sqrt(SS_res/(n - 3))
analysis.uncertainty: standard error of mu and I over the run's steady snapshots; parameter standard errors from the OLS covariance
analysis.viscosity: eta = mu(I_ref) P_ref / gamma_ref with I_ref = gamma_ref d50 / sqrt(P_ref/rho), d50 from the DEM, rho = 917 kg/m3; a P table (2, 5, 10, 20, 50 kPa) is reported as well so the reader sees the sensitivity to the declared reference pressure
analysis.reporting: all acceptance numbers are written to artifacts/rubble_rheology/summary.json and quoted verbatim in the report; an honest FAIL is not overwritten

stopping_rule: the production sweep stops when all 22 declared runs have completed or a run exceeds 20 minutes of wall time (then it is reported as incomplete, not replaced). The fit is computed once, after the full sweep; the rate ladder is not extended after seeing the acceptance result.
pilot_note: Single short pilot runs (N=220, not part of the acceptance dataset) were used only to choose the affordable rate ladder and the solid fraction at which the packing is load bearing (phi >= 0.82 gives P ~ 10 kPa). The acceptance thresholds are the battle-node values and were not tuned; pilot numbers are excluded from the fit.

amendments.status: written after sweep 1 (22 runs, archived in artifacts/rubble_rheology/sweep1) and before sweep 2
changes: compression element test made isochoric (the cell is stretched in x by the inverse of the piston factor so the solid fraction stays constant); sweep 1 used a confined cell that densified from phi=0.80 to phi>0.90 and never reached a steady stress ratio

primary calibration dataset = the two steady element tests (couette shear + isochoric plane-strain compression); the ice-channel scenario becomes an out-of-sample validation instead of a calibration point
sample size raised: 6 seeds for the two element tests, 4 seeds for the channel; shear strain 2.0 -> 3.0 and 12 snapshots per run
reasons: sweep-1 diagnostic: compression gave mu = 0.065-0.145 while shear gave 0.25-0.32 at the same I; the confined cell densifies to random close packing, so its stress ratio is not a material response (the solid fraction is not a controlled variable)

sweep-1 diagnostic: the channel scenario measures a drag-dominated, heterogeneous stress state in which the global velocity-profile slope is not a material shear rate (I ~ 1e-4 while mu ~ 0.09); it cannot calibrate a homogeneous constitutive law and is kept as a validation case
sweep-1 diagnostic: seed-to-seed scatter of mu at fixed rate was ~0.025, comparable with the trend over the ladder, so the estimator needs more averaging
unchanged: the quadratic model form mu = mu0 + alpha I + beta I^2

the pooled-over-the-calibration-dataset fit as the primary acceptance object (the archived sweep-1 pooled fit over all three scenarios is still reported as a diagnostic and fails: R^2 = 0.406, residual_std = 0.080)

amendments.attempt: P82W2-N02 (second mission on this physical node; the P82W4-N02 sweep is re-used only as the legacy reference, all numbers here are regenerated)
amendments.status: written BEFORE the production sweep of this attempt; the pilot rows below are the only data seen at writing time
driver_defects_fixed: the compression piston carried no wall velocity, so the wall-contact damping was evaluated against a static wall (ablation: P 7.3 -> 9.0 kPa, mu 0.2963 -> 0.3161 at the same run)

the compression shear rate was the nominal 2|eps_y|; the realised bulk rate measured from the velocity gradient is only 0.70-0.75 of the nominal one, so I was overstated by ~35% (the shear scenario already used a measured rate: the two element tests were therefore not on the same footing)

a third candidate fix (affine velocity increment on the isochoric x remap) was tested and REJECTED: it doubles the pressure (7.3 -> 17.6 kPa) and collapses mu to 0.063-0.093 because the engine's periodic images carry no box-rate term and the remap injects a spurious slip on the periodic seam. The x remap stays position-only and this is declared as a model-form limitation.
design_changes: two solid-fraction (pressure) levels per element test: shear phi in {0.82, 0.85}, compression phi in {0.80, 0.84}; three seeds per (case, rate); this widens the I lever arm and makes the pressure level an explicit controlled factor instead of a hidden confounder
seeds reduced from 6 to 3 per condition because the number of conditions doubled; the estimator's seed scatter is unchanged (mu SE 0.004-0.01 per condition)
channel scenario: phi = 0.80, 3 drift speeds x 2 seeds, still an out-of-sample validation (never a calibration point)
amendments.pilot_reading: phi=0.76 compression runs at P ~ 0.7 kPa (near-unjammed, 232 contacts) and is excluded from the production ladder; the production compression levels are 0.80 and 0.84 where P >= ~5 kPa. The pilot does NOT enter any fit.
unchanged: all five acceptance thresholds, the model form mu = mu0 + alpha I + beta I^2, no post-hoc outlier removal
primary acceptance object = pooled quadratic fit over the two element tests (condition means, seeds as replicates)
channel scenario is an out-of-sample validation, not a calibration point
